listing.name: Abuse 2025
listing.summary: Use a permitted existing Abuse player with its compatible game data.

steps.title: Keep the permitted working player and data together
steps.instruction: For an existing copy you are permitted to use, select abuse.exe on Windows or abuse on Linux with its game folder as the working directory. Keep its compatible data and libraries together; ABUSE_PATH overrides the asset root. The current release offers Windows and macOS packages; Linux here describes an already prepared native copy, not an offered Linux archive or a Portcove build. macOS uses the upstream application through the OS, not a private bundle binary.

steps.title: Back up the actual save directory
steps.instruction: The reviewed SDL code normally uses SDL_GetPrefPath("abuse", "data") for saves/settings: %APPDATA%/abuse/data on Windows, or $XDG_DATA_HOME/abuse/data (normally ~/.local/share/abuse/data) on Linux. ABUSE_SAVE_PATH overrides it; if preference-path creation fails upstream falls back to the current working directory. Preserve that actual location, custom levels/mods and the working data folder with the game closed. The local_save flag alone is not proof that saves are beside the executable.

steps.title: Retain upstream replacement and data ownership
steps.instruction: Registration leaves the external files untouched. You and upstream own updates and backups; Portcove supplies no managed backup or rollback. Upstream mentions a public-domain data subset, but its exact clean subset and compatibility with this release still need acceptance. Do not automatically replace mixed bundled assets or claim that a root code license covers music and soundfonts.

listing.download_block_reason: Fresh bundled-package acquisition remains held for the documented mixed/uncertain game-data, music and soundfont permissions. Reconsider after exact component grants or a compatible clean official data/package route is accepted. A conditional permitted-existing-copy route does not clear those assets.
